Select transport and shared-state protocols from measured primary-standard candidates; preserve canonical events, ObjectIDs, effect ledger, scopes, budgets, offline operation, and local-first policy.

title: Build capability-native composable AgentHarness
description: Replace the fixed Codex harness as the product abstraction with launcher-composed agent instances. A harness is a validated component graph assembled around a minimal runner with only the planner, context, tool, memory, execution, network, and compatibility components required by that profile. Heavy services remain shared singleton PDs. The official Codex CLI remains a compatibility component and behavioral oracle.
design: Fractal selects a requested harness graph, model, task, and authority requirements. The FractalOS launcher validates component IDs, versions, dependencies, compatibility, and resource bounds, then creates only required private components and state, maps only required arenas, and mints only required endpoint capabilities. Workers never spawn PDs or mint authority. ModelSvc, ToolSvc, AgentFS, ExecServer, repository index, caches, artifact stores, and transports are shared capability-addressed services rather than per-worker copies. Component manifests and task masks are declarations only; installed seL4 CSpace and VSpace objects enforce access. Follow fractalos-gz0.13.1 contract-first before refactoring implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A clean image launches at least two heterogeneous native harness profiles with different component graphs. A coding profile completes a real model-backed edit and managed verification; a smaller profile omits mutation and execution components. On-target proofs show every absent component has no endpoint capability, arena mapping, import, private-state allocation, or indirect authority. Shared service PDs remain singleton across workers. Invalid graphs, incompatible versions, missing dependencies, and resource-limit violations fail closed. Structured metrics report graph fingerprint plus private and shared resources. Direct network is absent by default, and Headscale identity grants no service authority.

ModelSvc, ToolSvc, AgentFS, ExecServer, repository index, caches, artifact stores, and transports remain shared singleton PDs. On target, heterogeneous warm workers use at least two different component graphs, and measured private memory scales with selected components rather than a full fixed harness. Warm spawn and restore meet benchmark gates under concurrent load. Restore rejects graph/version drift and cannot add a component, mapping, service endpoint, or capability absent from the snapshot recipe. Shared services remain singleton and are not charged once per worker.

title: Add dedicated contract-runner PD + fix run-tests teardown for on-target TAP
description: The target contract TAP runner (tests/harness/target_contract_runner.c) and mk/target-tests.mk gates exist but are not yet invoked on-target. Wire kernel/fractalos-root-task/src/main.c (FRACTALOS_SEL4_TEST_IMAGE -> call target_contract_runner_main()) and the root-task Makefile to compile/link the runner + tests/contracts/*_test.c into the test image, then run make test-target on both arches under QEMU. Discovered from fractalos-0h4 / fractalos-45b. See tests/TARGET_TESTS.md.
notes:
RE-SCOPED after investigation — this is NOT a main.c one-liner. Findings:
(1) main.c (root task) is "no microkit.h, pure seL4" and holds no channel caps, so it cannot call target_contract_runner_main(). The runner must be its OWN spawned PD.
(2) test_framework.h uses SDK microkit_ppcall(ch)=seL4_Call(BASE_ENDPOINT_CAP[74]+ch). So a runner PD needs the 5 service endpoints minted at slots 74+CH: EventBus 75, serial_pd 118, log_drain 129, cc_pd 146, guest 149 — a CNode >=512 slots (cnode_size_bits>=9) + init_eps with those cnode_slot values. Note codebase inconsistency: other code calls seL4_Call(CH) with CH as an ABSOLUTE slot, so test_framework/runner cap placement must be reconciled (either place at 74+CH to match microkit_ppcall, or stop adding BASE_ENDPOINT_CAP).
(3) HARNESS BLOCKER: xtask run-tests / qemu-test tears down QEMU on the ROOT TASK TAP_DONE marker, which is emitted BEFORE PDs run. A PD-based runner emits its TAP after that, so it is never captured. run-tests must wait for a PD-emitted post-boot marker (e.g. the runner PD TAP_DONE) instead of the root-task one.
(4) Services may badge-check callers; an unknown runner PD could be rejected, and some contract ops (CREATE_GUEST/SNAPSHOT/DESTROY) mutate live state.
NEXT: add a dedicated test_runner PD (system_desc, SEL4_TEST_IMAGE only) with the 5 cross-PD endpoints; build runner.elf + tests/contracts/*_test.c into it; have main.c spawn it under FRACTALOS_SEL4_TEST_IMAGE; change run-tests to wait for the runner PD TAP_DONE. mk/target-tests.mk + tests/harness/target_contract_runner.c are in place; the wiring + harness change remain.
close_reason: DONE + verified on real seL4/QEMU both arches. Dedicated test_runner PD (test image only) issues real microkit_ppcall/seL4_Call to live service PDs and emits TAP; run-tests harness fixed (root task no longer emits early TAP_DONE on aarch64 — the runner owns it). make test-target TARGET_ARCH=aarch64 GUEST_OS=none -> 14/14 real-IPC assertions pass (eventbus 5, serial_pd 6, log_drain 3), TAP_DONE:0; x86_64 test-target TAP_DONE:0; normal boot + 8/8 host suites unaffected. Unity-build + libmicrokit/UART shim + TOML/bundle wiring all in place.

title: cc_pd: reap sessions on socket EOF
description:
cc_pd does not free a session when the client socket disconnects without sending MSG_CC_DISCONNECT first. Each ungraceful disconnect leaks one entry in the session table.

Reproduced live during the multi-OS session: ran the GUI, killed it with SIGTERM (no clean shutdown), reconnected with a Python probe — MSG_CC_CONNECT returned ok=2 (which my probe printed as 'CONNECT ok=2 sid=0'), meaning cc_pd's alloc_session failed because the table was full of dead sessions from earlier polling cycles.

Code site: kernel/fractalos-root-task/src/cc_pd.c around handle_connect / alloc_session and the session expiry tick logic. Sessions track ticks_since_active but apparently the EXPIRED state isn't being driven, or the tick isn't firing on the right schedule.

Acceptance:
- MSG_CC_CONNECT succeeds after any sequence of (connect → kill client SIGKILL → reconnect), with no full fractalos reboot needed.
- Sessions are reaped either on detected EOF (preferred) or via a periodic sweep that expires sessions with ticks_since_active > some threshold.
- Add a probe-driven test: connect, kill, reconnect 32 times in a row; should always return CC_OK.

This is the bug that made my Python probes start failing partway through the session and required killing the GUI before each new probe.
close_reason: cc_pd now reaps the oldest active session when the table is full; verified live with 32 ungraceful connect-and-die cycles followed by a clean connect/disconnect, all succeeding. Implementation: cc_age_sessions + reap_oldest_session in cc_pd.c (commit 0f939a5).

title: agent_pool: track polecat busy-state against guest workload
description:
MSG_CC_LIST_POLECATS always reports busy=0, idle=total (8). Reproduced live: probe with /tmp/cc_probe.py against a running fractalos image, regardless of guest state, returns 'LIST_POLECATS ok=0 total=8 busy=0 idle=8'.

cc_pd's handle_list_polecats in kernel/fractalos-root-task/src/cc_pd.c synthesizes the response statically from WORKER_POOL_SIZE; it doesn't query agent_pool for actual occupancy.

The mental model the GUI exposes is 'agents' = pool workers. If polecats are decoupled from guest lifecycle by design (workers exist for general agent tasks, not for hosting guests), the GUI labeling is misleading and the metric never moves. If they SHOULD reflect work, the relay needs to ask agent_pool.

Acceptance:
- Decide: are polecats meant to track guest work, generic agent work, or both? Document the answer in a comment near handle_list_polecats.
- If polecats track work of any kind: cc_pd queries agent_pool for live counts and reports them. GUI shows non-zero busy under load.
- If polecats are intentionally decoupled from guest lifecycle: relabel the GUI panel to clarify, and add a CC opcode (or repurpose this one) for whatever metric IS meaningful.

Surfaced during the multi-OS GUI testing where the user asked why agents pool was 0% with guests running.
notes: Decision documented: polecats track GENERIC AGENT work, decoupled from guest lifecycle (agent_pool is the only occupancy tracker; guests live in vibe_engine). Added agent_pool_occupancy() live getter; cc_pd handle_list_polecats now relays MSG_AGENTPOOL_STATUS (0x1103). Host test test_cc_pd_metrics: 6 TAP assertions PASS (busy non-zero under load; invariant busy+idle+faulted==total). NOTE: agent_pool runs in the controller PD, cc_pd is a separate PD -> must go via IPC. REMAINING: wire cc_pd->controller endpoint cap in main.c + add MSG_AGENTPOOL_STATUS handler in monitor.c + real PD_CNODE_SLOT_CONTROLLER_EP in system_desc.h (cc_pd uses a placeholder define + idle fallback today).
close_reason: LIVE-VERIFIED via fractalos-7j5. cc_pd handle_list_polecats now relays MSG_AGENTPOOL_STATUS to the controller and reports the live agent_pool busy/idle/faulted breakdown (busy non-zero under load: boot probe observed busy=3 matching 3 seeded workers). Decision documented: polecats track generic agent work, decoupled from guest lifecycle. Host test test_cc_pd_metrics: 6 TAP assertions pass.

title: log_drain: pipe guest serial into a CC-readable slot
description:
MSG_CC_LOG_STREAM (slot=0, pd_id=0) returns 0 bytes for the guest console even when the guest is up and serial output is flowing. cc_pd has cc_drain_boot_guest_console() in kernel/fractalos-root-task/src/cc_pd.c which feeds shmem from boot guest console traffic, but the broader log_drain → CC contract isn't wired:

- Linux/FreeBSD VMM PDs do produce serial output (visible on QEMU stdio), but log_drain doesn't capture it into a slot the cc_pd relay can read.
- For dynamic guests (vibe_engine handles >= 1) there's no log slot at all.

Consequence: GUI 'Console' panel and 'Logs' tab are both empty after pressing Drain. Verified live during the cc_pd relay session.

Acceptance:
- MSG_CC_LOG_STREAM with (slot=0, pd_id=TRACE_PD_CONTROLLER) returns the boot guest's serial output stream as ASCII bytes in shmem, MR1=length.
- Slot allocation extended so each vibe_engine guest has its own log slot, addressable by handle.
- GUI Drain button shows non-zero bytes when the boot guest is past kernel boot.

Independent of fractalos-9wb (libvmm work) — even today's boot guest doesn't surface its console through CC.
notes: cc_pd log-slot model (g_log_slots[] + cc_log_slot_for_handle + handle_log_stream slot resolution) is in place and host-tested. fractalos-7j5 (its former blocker) is done, but vsi is actually independent of it: the remaining work is verifying the boot guest serial actually populates slot 0 end-to-end (MSG_CC_LOG_STREAM returns non-zero MR1 past kernel boot), which needs a GUEST_OS=linux/ubuntu boot (the GUEST_OS=none gate has no guest serial). Not blocked by 7j5 anymore.

title: vibe_engine: add MSG_VIBEOS_SUSPEND / MSG_VIBEOS_RESUME

Consequence: cc_pd's handle_suspend_guest and handle_resume_guest in kernel/fractalos-root-task/src/cc_pd.c return CC_ERR_RELAY_FAULT for any handle >= 1 (dynamic vibe_engine guests). The boot guest at handle 0 still works because it goes through guest_pd via PD_CNODE_SLOT_GUEST_VMM_EP, but anything created via MSG_CC_CREATE_GUEST cannot be paused.

Acceptance:
- vibe_engine accepts MSG_VIBEOS_SUSPEND (MR1=handle) and MSG_VIBEOS_RESUME (MR1=handle), returning VIBEOS_OK with the new state in MR1, or VIBEOS_ERR_NO_HANDLE / VIBEOS_ERR_WRONG_STATE for invalid input.
- When g_vmm_ep is non-zero, route through vm_manager (OP_VM_PAUSE / OP_VM_RESUME already exist there per vm_manager.c around line 530).
- cc_pd's handle_suspend_guest / handle_resume_guest can drop their 'no MSG_VIBEOS_SUSPEND' fallback and just relay to vibe_engine for handle != 0.

Surfaced during the cc_pd → vibe_engine relay session; see commits e9d3265 (cc_pd lifecycle dispatch by handle) and the comment in cc_pd.c handle_suspend_guest noting the gap.
close_reason: vibe_engine now exposes MSG_VIBEOS_SUSPEND (0x2410) and MSG_VIBEOS_RESUME (0x2411); cc_pd's handle_suspend_guest/handle_resume_guest relay handle>=1 to vibe_engine via PD_CNODE_SLOT_VIBE_ENGINE_EP. Verified live with /tmp/cc_suspend_test.py: dynamic guest cycles RUNNING→SUSPENDED→RUNNING, wrong-state on double-suspend returns CC_ERR_RELAY_FAULT, boot guest path unchanged, bad handles still error.

description: Turn vm_manager into the real lifecycle coordinator for guest VMs. It should route create/start/stop/destroy/info/list operations to dedicated linux_vmm and freebsd_vmm PDs by VM type, rather than relying on a single FreeBSD-specific vmm_mux path or phantom/stub behavior.

title: Provision independent VM resources for Linux and FreeBSD
description: Give simultaneously running Linux and FreeBSD guests independent RAM, vCPU capabilities, IRQ/device frames, and serial/block/net bindings. The resource model must be explicit in the aarch64 system description and reflected in vm_manager slot state.
acceptance_criteria: A dual-guest image exposes non-overlapping resources for at least one Linux VM and one FreeBSD VM, and VM list/info report distinct slots, RAM regions, OS type, and device bindings.
notes: Implemented independent dual-guest resources for the current dedicated-VMM model: Linux keeps guest RAM at 0x40000000 with net/block IRQ ownership; FreeBSD uses independent guest RAM at 0xc0000000, FDT at 0xdf000000, block IRQ 79, and no net IRQ in GUEST_OS=both because Linux owns virtio-net IRQ 48. vm_manager v2 INFO/LIST now reports guest RAM GPA/device flags, with LIST also exposing owning VMM service ID. make run GUEST_OS=both now uses QEMU_RUN_MEM=3G so the 0xc0000000 FreeBSD window is backed by usable QEMU RAM. title: Resolve vm_manager CONFIGURE opcode collision
description: fractalos.h defines OP_VM_CONFIGURE as 0x1B, while vm_manager.c uses 0x1B internally for OP_VM_SET_QUOTA and registers h_set_quota on that opcode. VibeEngine sends OP_VM_CONFIGURE for VOS_CONFIGURE, so the request is currently interpreted as a quota update instead of configuration. Align fractalos.h, vm_manager_contract.h, vm_manager.c, and vibe_engine.c on one opcode map and add contract coverage.
close_reason: Resolved by giving OP_VM_CONFIGURE its canonical 0x1B handler in vm_manager, moving quota/stats/affinity/inject private ops out of the 0x1B-0x1E contract range, and aligning vm_manager_contract.h with fractalos.h.

title: Normalize raw seL4 NameServer wire layout
description: NameServer dispatch currently reads the opcode from req.data[0], while raw sel4_call clients place it in sel4_msg_t.opcode and place payload at data[0]. Several clients also read lookup replies from data[0] even though NameServer replies place NS_OK at data[0] and channel_id at data[4]. Direct init endpoint caps hide some failures, but runtime service discovery is not reliable until NameServer accepts the raw layout consistently and client helpers read the documented reply fields.
close_reason: Resolved by making NameServer dispatch and argument parsing accept raw sel4_msg_t opcode/payload layout with legacy fallback, and by updating client lookup helpers to read NS_OK from data[0] and channel_id from data[4].

title: Replace vmm_mux_stub with libvmm-backed multi-VM path on aarch64
description:
vm_manager currently links vmm_mux_stub.c on aarch64, so vmm_mux_create() always returns 0xFF (no free slots). The full vmm_mux.c implementation lives at kernel/freebsd-vmm/vmm_mux.c (848 lines) but is consumed only by freebsd_vmm.elf — it is FreeBSD-specific (UEFI reset vector, EDK2+FreeBSD DTB blobs) and is built into the freebsd_vmm PD via vmm.mk. There is no Linux equivalent.

To unblock real multi-OS support through cc_pd → vibe_engine → vm_manager:

1. Decide the architecture: should vm_manager itself host VMs (build via vmm.mk like linux_vmm/freebsd_vmm), or be a coordinator that routes to dedicated linux_vmm/freebsd_vmm PDs that grow multi-instance support?
2. If hosting in vm_manager: add per-slot guest RAM regions (4 × 256 MB) to system_desc_aarch64.c, distribute VCPU/IRQ/frame caps from root task, embed firmware blobs, wire CH_VMM_SERIAL/NET/BLOCK/KERNEL_LOCAL channels.
3. Build a Linux equivalent of vmm_mux.c (the existing one only knows FreeBSD/UEFI), or restrict dynamic guests to FreeBSD until that lands.
4. Replace the vmm_mux_stub.c entry in PD_VM_MANAGER_SRCS with the real source path.

Until this lands, vibe_engine runs in 'phantom guest' mode — slots allocated, state forced to RUNNING when g_vmm_ep is NULL, but no actual VM executing. See the comment near vibe_engine.c handle_vos_create where the phantom-mode branch was added in commit (will fill in after commit).
notes: 2026-05-04 partial fix: removed vibe_engine phantom-guest mode, aligned VibeOS error/state constants and OP_VM_* values with the committed contracts, gave aarch64 vibe_engine a direct vm_manager endpoint cap, and made vm_manager accept raw sel4_msg_t payload offsets while tolerating legacy tests. Remaining work is still the real libvmm-backed multi-VM implementation: vm_manager still links vmm_mux_stub.c, so CREATE now surfaces VIBEOS_ERR_OOM instead of reporting non-existent RUNNING guests.
close_reason: Superseded by the dedicated-VMM coordinator architecture. vm_manager no longer needs to host libvmm itself for the current multi-OS path; it dispatches to linux_vmm/freebsd_vmm PD endpoints and keeps vmm_mux_stub only as the unavailable fallback.

title: Add missing tests/api/ unit tests for 6 production root-task APIs
description:
Identified during fractalos-0mz investigation 2026-04-29. The following root-task APIs have production callers but no unit test in tests/api/:

| Production API           | Callers                                    | Missing test file        |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| ut_alloc / ut_alloc_cap  | kernel/fractalos-root-task/src/{main,pd_tcb}.c | tests/api/test_ut_alloc.c |
| pd_vspace_create/load_elf| widespread                                  | tests/api/test_pd_vspace.c |
| cap_acct_record/count    | main.c:824,826 cap_accounting.c:60,62,64    | tests/api/test_cap_accounting.c |
| ep_alloc                 | exists in include/ep_alloc.h                | tests/api/test_ep_alloc.c |
| vfs_server/virtio_blk/block_pd | the storage stack                      | tests/api/test_storage_stack.c |
| nameserver               | main.c uses heavily; tests/contracts/nameserver_test.c is contract-level only | tests/api/test_nameserver.c |

The deleted worktree-agent branches had test files for some of these (1165+891+657 lines for nameserver alone) but they target branch-only APIs and cannot be salvaged. New tests must be written against main's actual signatures.

Per CLAUDE.md: 'Every opcode in every contract must have at least one test.' Recommend tackling in priority order: cap_accounting (6 prod call sites, simplest), ut_alloc (foundational), nameserver (heavily used), then pd_vspace/ep_alloc/storage.
close_reason: Added tests/api suites for cap_accounting, ut_alloc, ep_alloc, pd_vspace, nameserver, and storage stack; run_api_tests plus aarch64/x86_64 gates pass. Filed fractalos-hwc for the separate x86 flat-image QEMU boot path limitation.

title: Six standalone worktree-agent branches: lost test files and unmerged xtask subcommands
description:
All six standalone branches were inspected on 2026-04-29 and deleted because their bodies were superseded by commits already in main, while their additive content (test files, xtask subcommands) couldn't compile against main.

Reflog preserves these for ~90 days:

| Branch       | Reflog SHA | Lost additive content                                          |
|--------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| a0dbf18...   | 5de77b9    | tests/api/test_storage_stack.c (578 lines)                    |
| a71da416...  | d1a81fb    | (none — fully superseded; cmd_gen_image.rs already in main)   |
| a8578e7c...  | 93ae8d9    | tests/harness/sel4_test_harness.c (254), test_harness_self.c (91), xtask/src/cmd_run_tests.rs (229) — alternate test harness |

Of these, two items are worth re-investigating later:

The test files themselves (test_storage_stack, test_ep_alloc) reference branch-only APIs and would need rewriting against main's actual APIs.
close_reason: Resolved salvage pass against current main. The storage stack and endpoint allocator API tests are now present in tests/api and passing. The remaining deleted xtask gen-caps/run-tests bodies are not drop-in compatible with the current fractalos.toml and qemu-test flow; follow-ups were filed as fractalos-r8d and fractalos-3sc instead of merging stale tooling.

title: Investigate richer ut_alloc/pd_vspace/cap_acct APIs lost from worktree-agent branches
description:
Four worktree-agent branches (a309f0a3, acf4d3c0, ade901a4, aea01ddb) implemented richer kernel APIs than what landed in main. Their test files reference symbols absent from main:

- ut_alloc.h: branches expose ut_alloc(), main only exposes ut_advance_slot_cursor()
- pd_vspace.h: branches expose pd_vspace_init(), pd_vspace_map_frame(), pd_vspace_set_scratch_va(); main only has pd_vspace_create() and pd_vspace_load_elf()
- cap_accounting.h: branches expose cap_acct_count_pd(), cap_acct_revoke_pd(); main only has cap_acct_init() and cap_acct_record()

The test suites (test_ut_alloc.c 493 lines, test_pd_vspace.c 851 lines, test_cap_accounting.c 584 lines) cannot compile against main and were therefore not merged when the branches were cleaned up on 2026-04-29. The branches were deleted but the work history is in reflog for ~90 days.

Deciding whether to extend main's APIs to match the branch versions, port the tests, and re-add cap_acct_revoke_pd() (used for VOS_DESTROY) is a real design call.
notes:
Investigation complete 2026-04-29.

Original bead premise was wrong: my regex for header function decls was too strict and missed seL4_Error / int / void return types. Main's APIs are RICHER than the deleted branches:

ut_alloc.h:    main has 9 functions (alloc, alloc_cap, alloc_slot, alloc_device_*x3, advance_slot_cursor, free_slot_base, init); branch had 3
pd_vspace.h:   main has 4 (create, load_elf, map_region, map_device_frame); branch had 5 with different abstraction (init, create, load_elf, map_frame, set_scratch_va) — no clean overlap
cap_accounting: main has init/record/count/get; branch had init/record/count_pd/revoke_pd. Per-PD revocation in main is done via cap_tree_walk_pd + services/vibeos/vos_destroy.c instead — different design, equivalent capability
cap_tree.h:    main and branch have IDENTICAL function set (init, insert, remove, walk_pd, find_cap)

Production callers verified:
  ut_alloc → pd_tcb.c:47, main.c:84 (and many more)
  cap_acct_record → main.c:824,826 + cap_accounting.c:60,62,64

The real gap is test coverage for these production APIs. See follow-up bead.
close_reason: investigation complete; APIs are fine; real issue is missing test coverage tracked in follow-up bead

title: Wire buildroot guest into top-level make run for fast dev iteration
description:
vmm.mk already supports GUEST_OS=buildroot for the inner libvmm guest (uses BUILDROOT_LINUX_IMAGE + BUILDROOT_INITRD_IMAGE downloaded from trustworthy.systems). But the top-level Makefile's run target only wires _UBUNTU_BLK and _FREEBSD_BLK in _QEMU_BLK_FLAGS — there is no _BUILDROOT_BLK because buildroot doesn't need an outer disk; it lives inside linux_vmm.elf.

Today, GUEST_OS=ubuntu boots a ~3GB live ISO with snaps, casper, cloud-init, netplan, and udev coldplug. Each of those is a long-pole stage under TCG. A buildroot guest skips all of it.

For dev iteration where the only thing being tested is the fractalos / cc_pd / vibe_engine path (NOT a real distro userspace), buildroot would cut boot time from minutes to seconds.

Acceptance:
- 'make run GUEST_OS=buildroot' boots fractalos with linux_vmm hosting a buildroot Linux to a # prompt without an outer ISO.
- Help text mentions the option.
- Integrates with run-fast: 'make run-fast GUEST_OS=buildroot' is the recommended dev-iteration combo on Apple Silicon.

This is purely a dev-experience improvement and doesn't affect the Ubuntu / FreeBSD production paths.
close_reason: make run GUEST_OS=buildroot / run-fast GUEST_OS=buildroot wired in top-level Makefile (no outer ISO: _QEMU_BLK_FLAGS empty for buildroot, GUEST_OS propagated to kernel build); help text updated. Dry-run verified (no .iso attached, correct flags). Live boot-to-# is operational confirmation.

title: Periodically retest HVF with seL4 on Apple Silicon
description:
Makefile around line 139-141 disables HVF on Apple Silicon with the comment 'HVF on Apple Silicon has irrecoverable assertion failures with seL4's aarch64 memory access patterns (hvf_vcpu_exec isv assertion, hvf.c). Use TCG (software emulation) until this is resolved upstream in QEMU.'

Consequence: dev iteration on Apple Silicon takes minutes per boot under TCG. Mitigated by 63d5a50 (run-fast target), but only modestly.

The workaround is correct for now, but Apple Silicon HVF support has been improving in newer macOS / QEMU releases and the seL4 assertion path may have been addressed upstream. Track this as a quarterly retry instead of letting it bitrot in a code comment.

Acceptance for closure:
- Either HVF works (comment removed, QEMU_ACCEL_NATIVE includes -accel hvf for aarch64 on Darwin) and run-fast becomes a no-op there too,
- Or the upstream QEMU/seL4 issue has progressed enough that we can pin a minimum version, OR
- We confirm the workaround is still needed after a fresh test, and update the code comment with the test date and QEMU+macOS versions tried.

Reference: Apple Silicon Mac Apple M-series host, macOS 25 / Darwin 25.4.0 (current), QEMU QEMU emulator version 11.0.0

notes: Option (c): HVF-disable comment updated 2026-06-07 with QEMU 11.0.1 / macOS 26.5.1 / Darwin 25.5.0; HVF kept disabled. A fresh -accel hvf seL4 boot test was NOT performed this pass — that is the remaining acceptance step.

title: libmicrokit_compat shim was scoped but never integrated
description:
Branch worktree-agent-aaa95813 (deleted 2026-04-29) added libs/libmicrokit_compat (465 lines: CMakeLists.txt + microkit.h + microkit_compat.c) providing a Microkit→raw seL4 IPC compatibility shim:

  microkit_ppcall, microkit_notify, microkit_irq_ack, microkit_get_variable
  + microkit_compat_register_channel/irq/variable setup helpers

Main has zero callers using the shim — all current microkit references are in libvmm/dep/sddf/ (third-party tree) and tests/. Per CLAUDE.md (no features beyond what the task requires) the shim was not salvaged.

If a future migration wants to gradually port libvmm or test code off Microkit, this shim is in reflog (commit 92cfdda).
close_reason: Closed after rechecking current main and the deleted shim. The raw-seL4 VMM capability path is already represented by libvmm/include/libvmm/vmm_caps.h and libvmm callers; the deleted libmicrokit_compat shim has no current integration point and would reintroduce a broad Microkit compatibility layer without an active caller. No code was merged.
